title: Hugo's Sparkly Berry Map
markdown:
Hugo fixed toys in his workshop. It smelled of wood and sweet glue. He was very good at making toys, and happy feelings, too.

One sunny morning, Hugo found an old map. It had wiggly lines and round shapes, like secret drawings. The map, it was said, led to a Sparkleberry Bush. Its berries tasted like sunshine and giggles. But Hugo just looked confused.

“Which way do I go?” he wondered.

Bloom the bee buzzed by. Bzzzz-hello! she hummed. Hugo showed her the map. “These little pictures don’t help me!”

Then Miss Maple the robin landed on the windowsill. Her bright eyes twinkled. “Wondering about directions?” she asked.

Hugo showed her the map. “These pictures don’t tell me which way!”

Miss Maple blinked. “Have you seen my bird feeder, Hugo? The little pictures there tell me when it’s time to fill it with seeds.”

Hugo’s eyes widened. His spectacles shone. “Like special signs!” He looked at the map again. The wiggly line looked like the giggling creek! The big circle looked like the friendly old oak tree! And the pointy triangle? “The highest hill!” He sat for a moment, just looking. The wiggly line wasn’t just a line. It was the sound of the creek, bubbling over stones. The big circle wasn’t just a circle. It was the shade of the old oak, a place for rest.

Bloom buzzed with joy. Suddenly the map wasn’t just drawings. It was a language.

With Hugo holding the map and Bloom buzzing ahead, they followed the wiggly creek. Water chuckled over stones. The friendly oak made a round of shade, just like the circle on the paper. Then they climbed the pointy hill until the wind smelled sweet. And there it was! The Sparkleberry Bush, its tiny red berries catching the sunlight.

“We found it!” Hugo cheered.

Miss Maple nodded. “Maps use symbols, Hugo. They show us where to go. Like the signs on my feeder, but for big adventures.”

Hugo picked a sparkly berry. It tasted like sunshine and giggles, just as the map had promised. He looked again at the clever pictures: creek, oak, hill. Simple pictures, showing the way. He folded the map so the wiggly creek stayed on top. Bloom dusted pollen on his spectacles. Miss Maple flew back to her feeder, whose little pictures, like the map, only worked if you knew they meant something.
